introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 3 (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: three and a quarter hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR QUESTIONS in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing ONE question from SECTION B and TWO questions from Section C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each. Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references. Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed. Materials required: Topographic map, Graph Paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions in all : question ONE (obligatoire, 31 marks), ONE question de la Section B et TWO de la Section C ». `regles_choix` porte le minimum exprimable par section (B : 1 sur 2 ; C : 2 sur 4) ; la question 1 (Section A) est obligatoire donc sans règle ; la consigne complète (4 questions en tout) est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : Q1 = 31 (7+4+7+6+3+4), Q2 à Q7 = 23 chacune (Q2 : 5+3+2+3+8+2 ; Q3 : 12+2+3+4+2 ; Q4 : 6+6+6+5 ; Q5 : 4+10+9 ; Q6 : 6+12+5 ; Q7 : 5+10+8), soit 100 points pour les 4 questions à traiter ; aucun écart avec les totaux imprimés en page de garde. Pour les blocs à plusieurs items (Q1 a, c, d), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des points imprimés des items.

Sujet scanné de 5 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 7, carte topographique de Kumba avec sa légende, fond de carte du Cameroun) ; filigranes et bandeaux gcerevision.com ignorés. Contrairement à d'ordinaires Paper 3, la carte de Kumba et le fond de carte du Cameroun SONT dans le PDF et ont été recadrés en PNG (la carte, pivotée de 90 degrés sur la page, a été remise à l'endroit). Le papier millimétré n'est pas fourni.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level. Aucune statistique précise n'est avancée sauf celles du tableau imprimé de la Q3 ; les ordres de grandeur géographiques (pluviométries, altitudes, dates de création d'organismes) sont donnés de façon prudente et sont à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Q4 à Q7 : les corrigés de la Section C sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire géographique ; les ordres de grandeur (pluviométries de 1 500, 900 à 1 200, moins de 800 mm ; températures ; altitudes des plateaux et sommets), les dates approximatives (SODECOTON et SEMRY dans les années 1970, barrage de Lagdo au début des années 1980, centrales d'Édéa et de Song Loulou, réservoir de Lom Pangar dans les années 2010) et les exemples (parcs, festivals, jardins) sont donnés de façon prudente et à faire relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Q7(c) : « Western industrial triangle » n'est pas défini dans le sujet. Le corrigé le rapporte aux industries des villes des Hautes Terres de l'Ouest (Bafoussam, Dschang, Foumban, Bamenda) et le dit explicitement ; la délimitation exacte du « triangle » dans le programme du Board n'a pas pu être vérifiée : à faire relire par un enseignant de géographie avant mise en avant. Les exemples (UCCAO à Bafoussam, UNVDA à Ndop, thé de Ndu, artisanat de Foumban) sont des organismes ou sites réels, cités sans chiffres.
Q7(b) : exemples d'exploitation de l'eau (Sanaga : Édéa, Song Loulou, Lom Pangar, Nachtigal ; lac Tchad et système Logone-Chari) : dates et capacités volontairement non chiffrées.

questions.enonce_markdown: 7. (a) Briefly describe the relief characteristics of the Western Highlands. *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Western Highlands form a high, rugged area in the west of Cameroon, lying along the Cameroon volcanic line from the south-west to the north-east.
- *Plateaus at different levels:* the Bamenda, Bamileke and Bamoun plateaus, with altitudes of roughly 1,000 to 2,000 m, are separated by steep escarpments.
- *Volcanic mountains:* Mount Oku (about 3,000 m), the Bamboutos Mountains (above 2,500 m), Mount Manengouba and other volcanic peaks and cones rise above the plateaus; basalt lava has covered large areas.
- *Crater lakes and calderas:* many craters hold lakes (for example Lake Nyos, Lake Oku), with lava flows and fertile volcanic soils.
- *Escarpments and dissected slopes:* steep faulted escarpments (for example towards the Mbo plain and the Noun valley) and deeply cut valleys with waterfalls (for example on the Menchum River).
- *Basins and plains:* flat basins at the foot of the hills, such as the Ndop plain and the Noun valley, which flood in the rainy season.
- *Drainage:* the highlands form a water divide: rivers such as the Noun, the Mbam and the Wouri head toward the Atlantic, and other rivers head toward the Benue and the Cross River.

**Marking guide.** One mark for each characteristic described with an example, up to 5.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) Analyse the exploitation of any two water resources in Cameroon. *(10 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two resources, each analysed for 5 marks (extent, method of exploitation, benefits and problems).

**1. The River Sanaga (hydroelectric power) - 5 marks.**
- *Resource:* the Sanaga is the longest river and has the highest flow of Cameroon and falls strongly from the Adamawa Plateau to the Atlantic.
- *Exploitation:* power stations at Edea (from the 1950s) and Song Loulou (1980s), dams regulating the flow upstream (Mbakaou, Bamendjin, and the Lom Pangar reservoir built in the 2010s), and newer projects such as Nachtigal. The electricity supplies the national grid, industries (the aluminium smelter at Edea) and the towns.
- *Benefits:* cheap, renewable energy, industrial development, and rural electrification.
- *Problems:* low water in the dry season and drought reduce output, siltation, the cost of dams and transmission lines, displacement of people and ecological damage.

**2. Lake Chad and the Logone-Chari system (irrigation and fishing) - 5 marks.**
- *Resource:* the lake, the Logone and Chari rivers and their floodplain (Yaere) in the Far North.
- *Exploitation:* fishing (an important source of protein and income), irrigated rice (Maga dam and SEMRY schemes), flood-recession farming of dry-season sorghum, watering of cattle and domestic supply; international management by the Lake Chad Basin Commission.
- *Benefits:* food and income for a dense population in a dry region, and trade in fish and rice.
- *Problems:* the shrinking of the lake caused by drought and abstraction, silting of canals, floods, conflicts over land and water and the pressure on the fisheries.

**Other acceptable resources:** the Benue and Lagdo dam, the Atlantic Ocean (fishing, the Kribi port), mineral springs, groundwater and boreholes for domestic supply.

**Marking guide.** For each resource: description 1, exploitation 2, benefits 1, problems 1.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Using concrete examples, show that the Western industrial triangle is dominantly raw material-oriented. *(8 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*The question is taken to refer to the cluster of industries around the main towns of the Western Highlands (for example Bafoussam, Dschang, Foumban and Bamenda). The candidate should name the towns that his or her syllabus gives.*

**Meaning.** An industry is raw material-oriented when it is located close to its inputs, because the raw materials are bulky, perishable or lose weight in processing, so that transport costs are lower there than at the market.

**Evidence from concrete examples.**
1. *Coffee processing:* the Arabica coffee grown on the cool, fertile Western Highlands is hulled, graded and prepared for export in Bafoussam and near the producing areas (cooperatives such as UCCAO), because the cherries and parchment are bulky and the quality falls if they travel far.
2. *Food and agricultural processing:* the rice mills of the Ndop plain (UNVDA scheme), maize and cassava mills, and fruit, vegetable and palm-oil processing near the farms, depend on the abundant output of the highland farms.
3. *Wood, clay and craft industries:* sawmills and furniture workshops in Foumban and Bamenda use local timber, and brick, tile and pottery works use local clay; Foumban's bronze and wood handicraft uses local materials and skills.
4. *Tea and other estates:* the tea of the Ndu estate is processed on site.
5. *Supporting factors:* abundant farm labour and cheap hydroelectric power, but the key location factor is the raw material.

**Qualification (for balance).** Some industries are market-oriented (for example brewing and beverages, which serve the large population of the region, and light assembly using imported inputs) and the region's industrial base remains small compared with Douala, but the dominance of agro-processing shows the pull of raw materials.

**Marking guide.** Meaning 1, three concrete examples explained 6, conclusion 1.
